text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German debt prices wobbled in late trade and remained in positive territory with the help of firmer U.S. Treasuries, the market looked toppish and was at risk of coming off in the early part of next week. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.62, down 0/05 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilt futures were up but below the post-data highs inspired by a much lower than expected increase in U.S. non-farm payroll, gilts boosted by substantial buy orders after initial dip on profit-taking following news of Labour election win. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-05/32, up 12/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures were boosted by non-resident buying and shrugged off a decline in the U.S. unemployment rate to 4.9 percent, surprising some economists who expected a strong negative reaction. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.48, up 0.52 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds ended up after playing catch-up with futures following a one-day holiday, futures themselves ending down on retracement after climbing on Thursday. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.91, down 0.34 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries fell again in late morning trade as hopes for a budget agreement fades, tax cuts were key sticking point, the market said wrestling with significance of 4.9 pct jobless rate, with fall in jobless rate seen clouding outlook for Fed policy. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-18/32, down 03/32 from Thusday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.93 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended the Tokyo session higher as investors bought cash JGBs, "Cash JGBs, not futures, dominated activity today. The market's mood has improved as investors' buying was detected," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.51, up 0.04 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity remained subdued, ending a quiet week in the Eurobond market, crucial U.S. jobs data for April is due to be released today, which will be closely watched for inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy. In Britain, markets were absorbing the impact of a change in government after 18 years of Conservative rule. The Labour party was swept to power with a landslide victory, with a predicted majority of 179 seats in parliament.
